entries.why_wrong: `summary.total` is initialized to `0` right where `summary` is declared, so there's no `NaN` here — the numbers accumulate correctly. The real problem is that every push into `results` stores a reference to that one shared object, so all entries end up showing the same final total once the loop finishes.

Swapping `for...of` for an index-based loop wouldn't change anything, since the loop construct isn't what's causing the aliasing. `summary` is still created once outside the loop and the same reference still gets pushed on every pass, regardless of how you iterate.

Pushing `summary.total` would only paper over the symptom by dropping the `items` list entirely, and it still wouldn't give per-order snapshots — you'd just get the same final running total copied into every slot instead of an object. The fix needs a fresh object per iteration, not a narrower one.
